result.title: Drug-coated balloon versus standard percutaneous transluminal angioplasty for the treatment of superficial femoral and popliteal peripheral artery disease: 12-month results from the IN.PACT SFA randomized trial
result.authors: Tepe G, Laird J, Schneider P, Brodmann M, Krishnan P, Micari A, Metzger C, Scheinert D, Zeller T, Cohen DJ, Snead DB, Alexander B, Landini M, Jaff MR; IN.PACT SFA Trial Investigators
result.population: 331 patients with intermittent claudication or ischaemic rest pain from atherosclerotic disease of the superficial femoral and/or proximal popliteal artery, randomised 2:1 to paclitaxel drug-coated balloon (n=220) vs standard PTA/POBA (n=111); prospective, multicentre, single-blinded RCT. The anchor draws on the PTA (plain balloon) control arm.
result.endpoint_as_reported: clinically driven target lesion revascularization at 12 months
result.evidence_quote: "The rate of clinically driven target lesion revascularization was 2.4% in the DCB arm in comparison with 20.6% in the PTA arm (P<0.001)."
result.notes:
CONFIRMED EXACTLY, no change needed. The author's justification ("IN.PACT SFA control arm 12-month CD-TLR 20.6%") is an accurate, correctly attributed quotation of the primary source. I opened the Europe PMC core record for PMID 25472980 (full indexed abstract) and, independently, the American College of Cardiology trial summary page; both give PTA-arm 12-month clinically driven TLR = 20.6% and DCB-arm = 2.4%. Endpoint wording in the source is exactly "clinically driven target lesion revascularization", i.e. the model's intended endpoint — no endpoint conversion was involved. Companion figure in the same abstract: 12-month primary patency 82.2% (DCB) vs 52.4% (PTA).

Two caveats for the model rather than for this citation:
(1) Evidence-tier note. This is a Level 1 RCT control arm with adjudicated endpoints (CEC-adjudicated, blinded patients, independent core labs), so trust weight 1 is defensible. But 20.6% is at the HIGH end of the POBA literature for femoropopliteal disease. Other pivotal DCB RCTs report lower 12-month CD-TLR in their PTA control arms (LEVANT 2 and ILLUMENATE Pivotal control arms are in the roughly 12-17% range from memory — I did NOT open those papers in this task, so treat those numbers as unverified). If the model's SFA-POBA anchor is meant to represent POBA generally rather than "the IN.PACT SFA control arm specifically", a pooled/meta-analytic value would likely land somewhat below 20.6% and the weight on this single-trial value might reasonably be softened. As written, however, the anchor and its stated justification are internally consistent and correctly sourced.
(2) Lesion-length dependence. IN.PACT SFA enrolled relatively short lesions (mean roughly 6-9 cm), so this POBA failure rate is not transferable to long-segment or heavily calcified SFA disease, where POBA CD-TLR is higher. Worth flagging if the model applies the anchor across lesion complexity strata.

The AHA/Circulation full-text page itself (ahajournals.org) returned HTTP 403 and PubMed returned only a cookie banner, so the verbatim abstract text above came from the Europe PMC REST core record, which mirrors the indexed publisher abstract; the ACC page served as the independent cross-check of both percentages. DOI, PMID, volume and pages were all read off the retrieved record, not reconstructed.

result.population: 331 patients with intermittent claudication or ischaemic rest pain attributable to superficial femoral / proximal popliteal artery disease, randomised 2:1 to paclitaxel drug-coated balloon vs standard PTA; mean lesion length 8.94 +/- 4.89 cm (DCB) and 8.81 +/- 5.12 cm (PTA); total occlusions 25.8% vs 19.5%

result.title: Drug-coated balloon versus standard percutaneous transluminal angioplasty for the treatment of superficial femoral and popliteal peripheral artery disease: 12-month results from the IN.PACT SFA randomized trial
result.authors: Tepe G, Laird J, Schneider P, Brodmann M, Krishnan P, Micari A, Metzger C, Scheinert D, Zeller T, Cohen DJ, Snead DB, Alexander B, Landini M, Jaff MR; IN.PACT SFA Trial Investigators
result.notes: Anchor verified exactly, and the author's justification string is correct in every part: device (IN.PACT Admiral paclitaxel DCB), bed (SFA/proximal popliteal), endpoint (clinically driven TLR), timepoint (12 months), value (2.4%) and venue (Circulation 2015). Evidence level is the best available: prospective, multicentre, single-blinded RCT, 2:1 randomisation, n=331, independent adjudication, so trust weight 1 is defensible. Source record read via the Europe PMC REST core record for PMID 25472980 (full authors, volume/pages, DOI and complete abstract); the AHA journals full text (ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.114.011004) returned HTTP 403 and PubMed's HTML returned only a cookie notice, so the verbatim quote above comes from the abstract as served by Europe PMC, not from the article body. Two caveats for the model rather than for the citation. (1) In IN.PACT SFA the 2.4% CD-TLR is a secondary endpoint; the trial's primary efficacy endpoint was primary patency (82.2% DCB vs 52.4% PTA), i.e. freedom from restenosis OR CD-TLR. If other anchors in the model are populated from primary-patency-loss or binary-restenosis figures, this anchor is not on the same scale as those, since loss of primary patency at 12 months here was ~17.8% versus CD-TLR 2.4% in the same arm. (2) 2.4% is the best-in-class figure for femoropopliteal DCB, not a class-average. Other pivotal femoropopliteal DCB RCTs report materially higher 12-month TLR (e.g. LEVANT 2 / Lutonix, Rosenfield et al., NEJM 2015, reported freedom from TLR of roughly 87.7% in the DCB arm, i.e. TLR near 12%). I did NOT open that paper in this check - the figure came from a search snippet only - so it must not be cited as verified. If the anchor is meant to represent the dcb_periph class in the SFA generically rather than the IN.PACT device specifically, it is optimistic by roughly a factor of 3-5 and should be re-derived from a meta-analysis; if it is meant device-specifically, it is correct as written and needs no change.

result.title: Randomized Trial of Stent versus Surgery for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis
result.authors: Rosenfield K, Matsumura JS, Chaturvedi S, Riles T, Ansel GM, Metzger DC, Wechsler L, Jaff MR, Gray W (ACT I Investigators)
result.population: 1453 patients randomised 3:1 (1089 stenting / 364 endarterectomy), age <=79 y, severe ASYMPTOMATIC carotid stenosis, NOT at high risk for surgical complications; 62 US sites, 2005-2013. Stenting arm used closed-cell tapering nitinol stent (Xact, Abbott Vascular) with distal embolic protection (Emboshield / Emboshield NAV6) - i.e. exactly the car_closed device class.
result.endpoint_as_reported: Freedom from clinically driven target-lesion revascularisation (prespecified secondary endpoint at 6 and 12 months)
result.reported_value: Freedom from clinically driven target-lesion revascularisation at 1 year: 99.4% stenting vs 97.4% endarterectomy (P=0.005). This equals a 12-month CD-TLR rate of 0.6% in the closed-cell carotid stent arm. (At 6 months: 99.8% vs 99.7%, P=0.72, i.e. CD-TLR 0.2%.)
result.evidence_quote: "at 1 year, the rates were 99.4% and 97.4%, respectively (P=0.005)" - Results, freedom from clinically driven target-lesion revascularization
result.notes:
VERDICT: the anchor is roughly 6x too high; it should be lowered from 3.5% to ~0.6%.

WHAT WENT WRONG IN THE JUSTIFICATION: the author's note ("1-y in-stent restenosis/TLR of a few percent") conflates two different endpoints. Duplex-defined binary in-stent restenosis after CAS is indeed of the order of a few percent in the first 1-2 years, but the model's endpoint is 12-month CLINICALLY DRIVEN TLR, which in carotid is far lower because most angiographic/duplex restenosis in the carotid bed is asymptomatic and not revascularised. Do not carry the restenosis magnitude into the CD-TLR slot.

PRIMARY SOURCE USED (highest tier available, an RCT of exactly this device class): ACT I, NEJM 2016;374:1011-1020. CD-TLR is a PRESPECIFIED protocol secondary endpoint, and the stenting arm used a closed-cell nitinol stent (Xact) with distal protection, so device class and arterial bed match the anchor exactly. Verbatim from the paper's Methods: "For stenting, closed-cell, nitinol stents with a tapering diameter (Xact, Abbott Vascular) were [used]". 12-month CD-TLR = 100% - 99.4% = 0.6%.

CORROBORATION FROM CONTEMPORARY PIVOTAL SINGLE-ARM CAS TRIALS (searched, abstract-level only, not opened in full - treat as supporting context, not as the cited source):
- C-GUARDIANS (CGuard micronet-covered stent, JACC Cardiovasc Interv 2025): TLR through 1 year 1.0% (3/299).
- PERFORMANCE II (JACC Cardiovasc Interv 2024): no clinically driven target lesion revascularisations at 12 months (0%).
- PERFORMANCE I: no TLR or in-stent restenosis through 12 months.
All three sit in the 0-1% band, consistent with ACT I and inconsistent with 3.5%.

CAVEATS ON GENERALISABILITY (reason I suggest weight 0.85 rather than 0.9+): ACT I enrolled only ASYMPTOMATIC, average-surgical-risk, <=80-year-old patients, so it is the favourable end of the CAS spectrum; symptomatic and high-risk cohorts and real-world registries may run somewhat higher, and CD-TLR also depends on how aggressively surveillance duplex triggers reintervention. Even so, no source I found puts 12-month CD-TLR for closed-cell carotid stents anywhere near 3.5%. If you want to hedge for symptomatic/registry populations, 0.008-0.010 is defensible; 0.006 is the value the best RCT actually reports.

TOOL NOTE: nejm.org and pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov both refused direct fetch (403 / cookie wall); I read the full ACT I article text from a fetched PDF of the published NEJM article and confirmed bibliographic fields (volume 374, issue 11, pages 1011-1020) via the Crossref API for DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1515706 and the PMID via NCBI esearch. No field below is guessed.

result.reported_value: Symptom-driven target lesion revascularization 17% in the PTCA (balloon-only) arm vs 12% in the stent arm at 1 year (not statistically significant). Related 1-year composites in the same arm: 70% free of death/MI/any revascularization (i.e. 30% with an event), 74% free of death/MI/TLR (i.e. 26%).
result.endpoint_as_reported: "Symptom-driven target lesion revascularization" at 1 year (the trial's own wording); the trial's primary endpoint was 6-month angiographic restenosis (>=50% diameter stenosis), reported separately as 42.1% PTCA vs 31.6% stent in the index NEJM publication.
result.population: 407 patients with symptomatic ischaemic heart disease and new (de novo) lesions of native coronary arteries, randomised to Palmaz-Schatz stent vs conventional PTCA; enrolled Jan 1991 - Feb 1993; balloon-only arm n=202-207.
result.evidence_quote: "Symptom-driven target lesion revascularization occurred in 12% of the stent group versus 17% of the PTCA group."
result.title: One-year follow-up of the Stent Restenosis (STRESS I) Study
result.authors: George CJ, Baim DS, Brinker JA, Fischman DL, Goldberg S, Holubkov R, Kennard ED, Veltri L, Detre KM
result.notes:
CONCLUSION: the anchor value of 32% is an endpoint mismatch, not a data error. 30-40% is the correct range for 6-month ANGIOGRAPHIC BINARY RESTENOSIS after balloon-only coronary angioplasty, but 12-month clinically driven TLR in the same patients is roughly half that. The author's justification ("1-y restenosis 30-40%, TLR of that order") makes exactly the conversion the model's own rules forbid.

PRIMARY SOURCE (opened and read verbatim via NCBI efetch): STRESS I 1-year follow-up, an RCT (evidence tier 1). Verbatim abstract gives symptom-driven TLR 17% in the balloon arm at 1 year. The index publication (Fischman et al., N Engl J Med 1994;331:496-501) reported the 6-month angiographic restenosis of 42.1% (PTCA) vs 31.6% (stent) and 6-month ischaemia-driven target-lesion revascularisation 15.4% vs 10.2% - note that the "31.6%" often quoted as a balloon-era number is in fact the STENT arm's restenosis rate.

CORROBORATING RCT (also opened, PMID 8557891, DOI 10.1016/0735-1097(95)00473-4): Macaya C et al., "Continued benefit of coronary stenting versus balloon angioplasty: one-year clinical follow-up of Benestent trial", J Am Coll Cardiol 1996;27(2):255-261. At 1 year, repeat angioplasty was required in 21% of the balloon arm vs 10% of the stent arm (p=0.001); the 1-year composite major-event rate was 31.5% balloon vs 23.2% stent (p=0.04). The 31.5% composite MACE is almost certainly where the 32% figure came from - it is a composite of death, stroke, MI, CABG and repeat intervention, not CD-TLR.

So the defensible 12-month clinically driven TLR band for balloon-only coronary PCI is 0.17-0.21 (STRESS I 17%, BENESTENT 21%). I have put 0.17 in suggested_value because that is the single source whose endpoint wording matches the model's endpoint most exactly ("symptom-driven target lesion revascularization", 12 months); if the model prefers a pooled two-RCT midpoint, 0.19 is also defensible. 0.32 should not be retained for a CD-TLR/TLF anchor.

CAVEATS worth carrying in the model: (1) both trials used narrow selection (stable angina, de novo, vessels mostly >=3.0 mm) and the authors of STRESS I explicitly flag "low statistical power, narrow patient selection"; (2) in small vessels the gap widens - STRESS small-vessel analysis (Savage MP et al., J Am Coll Cardiol 1998;31(2):307-311, PMID 9462572, also opened) reports 6-month restenosis 55% in the balloon arm vs 34% stent, with 1-year event-free survival 67% vs 78%, so a small-vessel-weighted POBA anchor would be higher than 0.17; (3) in in-stent restenosis, POBA 12-month TLR is much higher again, so a single coronary POBA anchor cannot serve both de novo and ISR use cases - consider splitting the anchor.

DATA-HYGIENE WARNING: search-engine summaries returned a spurious "27.3% TLR in the PTCA group vs 17.2% stent (p=0.008)" attributed to STRESS; I checked both the STRESS I 1-year abstract and the STRESS small-vessel abstract directly and neither contains those figures. Do not propagate that number. Weight raised from 0.6 to 0.8: two independent RCTs, adjudicated clinical endpoints, direct endpoint match, but historical-era and narrow population prevent a higher weight.

result.title: Biodegradable Polymer Versus Polymer-Free Ultrathin Sirolimus-Eluting Stents in Complex Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Post Hoc Analysis of the Stent Arm Registry From the HOST-IDEA Randomized Trial
result.authors: Park SH, Han JK, Yang S, Hwang D, Kang J, Yang HM, Park KW, Kang HJ, Koo BK, Cho JM, Cho J, Bang DW, Lee JH, Lee HC, Kim KJ, Chun WJ, Seo WW, Park WJ, Park SM, Kim YH, Kim HS
result.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
result.population: Patients undergoing PCI with third-generation ultrathin-strut sirolimus-eluting stents (Orsiro biodegradable-polymer SES or Coroflex ISAR polymer-free SES) in the HOST-IDEA randomised trial; propensity-score-matched 546 per stent group, of whom 336 underwent complex PCI (>=3 stents, >=3 lesions/vessels, bifurcation, total stent length >=60 mm, left main PCI, or heavy calcification)
result.endpoint_as_reported: Target lesion failure (TLF) at 1 year — composite of cardiac death, target vessel myocardial infarction, and clinically driven target lesion revascularization
result.reported_value: Complex PCI overall 5.7% vs noncomplex 1.3% (P<0.01); within complex PCI, Coroflex ISAR polymer-free SES 8.9% vs Orsiro biodegradable-polymer SES 2.4% (HR 3.74, 95% CI 1.24-11.26; P=0.02)
result.evidence_quote: "Complex PCI exhibited a significant association with a higher risk of TLF compared with noncomplex PCI (5.7% versus 1.3%, P<0.01)"
result.notes: The asserted 12.0% is materially too high; the justification "1-y TLF clusters at 10-14%" is not supported by any source I could open. Primary source (opened, Europe PMC core record with full abstract): HOST-IDEA stent-arm post hoc analysis, the only study I found that reports 12-month TLF specifically for ultrathin-strut DES stratified by PCI complexity, where complexity is defined largely by the same features the anchor names (total stent length >=60 mm, heavy calcification, multivessel/multistent). Complex-PCI TLF was 5.7% pooled across the two ultrathin platforms, and 12% lies outside even the worse-performing arm (Coroflex ISAR 8.9%). Corroboration (also opened, Europe PMC core record): Ajmera P et al., "Twelve months clinical outcomes of ultrathin strut sirolimus-eluting stent in real-world Indian patients with coronary artery disease," Am J Cardiovasc Dis 2022;12(5):262-271, PMID 36419862 — 1269 consecutive patients, "73.2% lesions were complex B2/C type", 12-month "cumulative incidence of TLF was 5.75%" with "1.72% CD-TLR", and 7.10% TLF in the diabetic subgroup. So the complex/diabetic ultrathin-DES band at 12 months is roughly 5-9% for TLF, and far lower (~2%) for CD-TLR alone. Recommend changing the anchor to 0.057 (5.7%) as a TLF-basis value; if the model needs a diabetes-weighted complex figure, 0.07 (7.1%, verified diabetic subgroup) is the defensible upper option, and 0.089 is the ceiling seen in the worst ultrathin arm. Caveats on weight: the HOST-IDEA figure is a post hoc, propensity-matched analysis rather than a prespecified randomised comparison, complex-PCI event counts are small (336 patients), and the two ultrathin platforms diverge widely (2.4% vs 8.9%), so platform choice drives the number as much as lesion complexity does. Also note the endpoint mismatch risk: if the model elsewhere prefers CD-TLR, the correct value would be substantially lower than any TLF figure here (registry CD-TLR 1.72%), so do not reuse 0.057 as a CD-TLR anchor. One important non-match to flag: BIOSCIENCE's prespecified diabetes subgroup (Iglesias JF et al., J Am Heart Assoc 2019;8(22):e013607, DOI 10.1161/JAHA.119.013607, PMID 31696762, also opened) reports 5-year, not 12-month, TLF (31.0% BP-SES vs 25.8% DP-EES in diabetes) — that paper must not be cited for a 12-month anchor. PubMed and PMC HTML were blocked (cookie/reCAPTCHA walls) and Europe PMC's article page returned 403; the Europe PMC REST API records were the readable route and are what I actually read, so all figures above come from full abstracts, not from search-result snippets.

result.title: Nitinol stent implantation versus balloon angioplasty for lesions in the superficial femoral artery and proximal popliteal artery: twelve-month results from the RESILIENT randomized trial
result.authors: Laird JR, Katzen BT, Scheinert D, Lammer J, Carpenter J, Buchbinder M, Dave R, Ansel G, Lansky A, Cristea E, Collins TJ, Goldstein J, Jaff MR; RESILIENT Investigators
result.population: 206 patients, 24 US/European centres, intermittent claudication with obstructive SFA/proximal popliteal lesions, randomised 2:1 to primary self-expanding bare nitinol stent (LifeStent) vs PTA; mean total lesion length 71 mm (stent arm) — "moderate-length lesions" in the authors' own wording; NCT00673985
result.endpoint_as_reported: "freedom from target lesion revascularization" at 12 months (stent arm 87.3%), i.e. 12-month TLR 12.7%; the abstract does not use the words "clinically driven", so strict CD-TLR wording is not confirmed from the text read
result.reported_value: Freedom from TLR at 12 months 87.3% in the nitinol stent arm vs 45.1% with angioplasty (P<0.0001) → 12.7% TLR in the stent arm
result.evidence_quote: "At 12 months, freedom from target lesion revascularization was 87.3% for the stent group"
result.notes: PRIMARY SOURCE FOUND AND OPENED (tier 1: RCT). RESILIENT is the randomised pivotal trial of primary bare nitinol self-expanding stenting in moderate-length SFA/proximal popliteal lesions; its stent arm gives 12-month TLR of 12.7% (100 - 87.3), which supports the asserted 13.0% essentially exactly. Refinement: use 0.127 rather than 0.130 if you want the trial number verbatim. Two caveats worth recording in the model. (1) Endpoint wording: RESILIENT reports "freedom from target lesion revascularization" and the abstract does not label it clinically driven, so this is TLR, not confirmed CD-TLR; I did not convert between endpoints. Note also that in RESILIENT bailout stenting was counted as a TLR and as loss of primary patency — that penalises the PTA arm only, not the stent arm, so the 12.7% figure is unaffected. (2) Heterogeneity across bare nitinol pivotal trials is real and mostly downward with later devices: COMPLETE SE (Laird et al., J Endovasc Ther 2014;21(2):202-12, PMID 24754279, opened) states "clinically driven target lesion revascularization (TLR) was required in 8.4% of patients at 12 months" with 12-month primary patency 72.6% — i.e. true CD-TLR in a contemporary single-arm IDE trial is roughly 8-9%, not 13%. DURABILITY II (Matsumura et al., J Vasc Surg 2013;58(1):73-83.e1, PMID 23642924, opened) covers longer lesions (core-lab mean 89 mm) and reports 12-month KM primary patency 77.2% but no 12-month TLR/CD-TLR rate in its abstract, so it cannot anchor this cell. Practical reading: 13.0% is defensible as a moderate-length bare nitinol TLR anchor with RESILIENT behind it, but if the model's endpoint is strictly clinically driven TLR the honest range is about 8-13% depending on device generation and lesion length, with RESILIENT at the upper end and COMPLETE SE at the lower end. Weight raised only modestly (0.7 to 0.8): the number is now backed by a real RCT rather than an expert guess, but the RCT/CD-TLR endpoint mismatch and the 8.4% contemporary comparator argue against higher confidence. No DOI, PMID, volume or page was guessed; all bibliographic fields came from the NCBI eutils record I retrieved. The publisher HTML at ahajournals.org returned HTTP 403, so verification is from the full MEDLINE abstract text plus the Europe PMC core record (10.1161/circinterventions.109.903468, pages 267-276), both of which I opened.

result.reason:
Could not refute; the citation survives adversarial checking on all three axes.

1) CITATION RESOLVES. Europe PMC core record for PMID 25472980 returns exactly the proposed metadata: Tepe G, Laird J, Schneider P, Brodmann M, Krishnan P, Micari A, Metzger C, Scheinert D, Zeller T, Cohen DJ, Snead DB, Alexander B, Landini M, Jaff MR; IN.PACT SFA Trial Investigators — "Drug-coated balloon versus standard percutaneous transluminal angioplasty for the treatment of superficial femoral and popliteal peripheral artery disease: 12-month results from the IN.PACT SFA randomized trial", Circulation 2015;131(5):495-502, DOI 10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.114.011004. No author-list drift, no year/volume/page drift, DOI and PMID agree. (PubMed's own page returned only a cookie wall, so I used the Europe PMC core record plus an independent web cross-check rather than the finder's single URL.)

2) NUMBER CONFIRMED. The offered quote is verbatim from the published abstract: "The rate of clinically driven target lesion revascularization was 2.4% in the DCB arm in comparison with 20.6% in the PTA arm (P<0.001)." Independently corroborated outside the abstract (Endovascular Today's coverage of the 1-year IN.PACT SFA results reports the same 2.4% vs 20.6% CD-TLR and 82.2% vs 52.4% primary patency). The 20.6% is not a transposition of any neighbouring figure in the paper — the other abstract numbers are 82.2%/52.4% (primary patency), 1.4%/3.7% (vessel thrombosis), 8.94/8.81 cm (lesion length), 25.8%/19.5% (total occlusions).

3) LENS 2 — ENDPOINT. The quoted 20.6% is explicitly clinically driven TARGET LESION revascularization at 12 months, i.e. CD-TLR, which is the anchor's endpoint. It is NOT the primary patency endpoint (that is the 52.4% figure, a composite of freedom from restenosis OR CD-TLR), NOT binary/duplex restenosis, NOT target VESSEL revascularization (CD-TVR appears only inside the separate primary safety composite), and NOT MACE. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01175850 independently lists "time to first clinically-driven TLR" at 12 months as a prespecified outcome, so the endpoint is prespecified rather than post hoc. Timepoint is 12 months as asserted.

4) LENS 2 — POPULATION. Registry official title: "Randomized Trial of IN.PACT Admiral Drug Coated Balloon vs Standard PTA for the Treatment of SFA and Proximal Popliteal Arterial Disease"; target vessel is the superficial femoral and/or proximal (above-knee) popliteal artery; enrollment 331 actual; control arm is non-coated balloon angioplasty, i.e. POBA. This matches the anchor's arterial bed (femoropopliteal/SFA) and device class (plain balloon). The 20.6% is drawn from the control arm, which is the correct arm for an SFA-POBA anchor. Lesion characteristics in the PTA arm are ordinary de novo femoropopliteal disease — mean lesion length 8.81 +/- 5.12 cm, 19.5% total occlusions — not an atypical subset (not in-stent restenosis, not a long-CTO-only or below-knee cohort), so no population mismatch.

Two caveats that fall short of refutation and should simply be stated if the anchor is described precisely: (a) the cohort is SFA AND/OR proximal popliteal, not SFA-only, so an anchor labelled purely "SFA" is slightly narrower than the source population; (b) both arms permitted provisional/bailout stenting, so the control is POBA-with-provisional-stenting rather than balloon-only in every case — the standard construction for this trial class. I could not open the Circulation full text (ahajournals.org and evtoday.com were both blocked by domain policy), so I could not confirm from the primary PDF whether 20.6% is a crude event rate or a Kaplan-Meier estimate; the abstract states it as a rate. That is a precision detail, not a contradiction of the value, endpoint, timepoint or population.

result.title: Drug-eluting balloon versus standard balloon angioplasty for infrapopliteal arterial revascularization in critical limb ischemia: 12-month results from the IN.PACT DEEP randomized trial
result.authors: Zeller T, Baumgartner I, Scheinert D, Brodmann M, Bosiers M, Micari A, Peeters P, Vermassen F, Landini M, Snead DB, Kent KC, Rocha-Singh KJ; IN.PACT DEEP Trial Investigators
result.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
result.population: 358 patients with critical limb ischaemia and infrapopliteal (below-the-knee) lesions, randomised 2:1 to IN.PACT Amphirion paclitaxel drug-eluting balloon vs standard PTA; prospective, multicentre, independent clinical event adjudication plus angiographic and wound core laboratories.
result.endpoint_as_reported: Clinically driven target lesion revascularization (CD-TLR) at 12 months (co-primary efficacy endpoint alongside late lumen loss)
result.reported_value: 9.2% CD-TLR in the drug-eluting balloon arm vs 13.1% in the PTA arm (p = 0.291)
result.evidence_quote: "Primary efficacy results of IA-DEB versus PTA were CD-TLR of 9.2% versus 13.1% (p = 0.291)"
result.notes:
VERDICT: the asserted 12.0% is not reported by any single source; the best-ranked source reports 9.2%. The author's justification range ("around 10-15%") is directionally reasonable but no trial lands on 12.0%, and the RCT evidence is markedly heterogeneous.

WHAT I OPENED (all read, not inferred):
1. IN.PACT DEEP (Zeller et al., JACC 2014;64:1568-76, PMID 25301459, DOI 10.1016/j.jacc.2014.06.1198) - PRIMARY SOURCE. This is the only below-the-knee DCB RCT I could confirm that reports the model's exact endpoint (CD-TLR) at exactly 12 months with independent clinical event adjudication, and the largest (n=358, all CLTI). DCB arm 12-month CD-TLR = 9.2% (PTA 13.1%, p=0.291, i.e. no significant benefit). Read via the Europe PMC core record; the PubMed HTML page returned only a cookie notice, and jacc.org dropped the connection.
2. IN.PACT BTK (Liistro, Weinberg, Almonacid Popma, Shishehbor, Deckers, Micari; EuroIntervention 2022, DOI 10.4244/EIJ-D-21-00444) - opened the article page. NOT usable for this anchor: its primary endpoint is 9-month late lumen loss, and the paper explicitly states follow-up "will continue to be followed up to 12, 24 and 36 months" - no 12-month CD-TLR published in that report. Only a safety note (3 deaths PTA, 1 DCB, no major target-limb amputations to 12 months).
3. Lutonix BTK RCT (n~440, Mustapha et al.) - the peer-reviewed publication I opened (J Invasive Cardiol 2019;31(8):205-211, PMID 31368893, DOI 10.25270/jic/19.3108.205) reports only the 6-MONTH primary endpoint and states CD-TLR was "statistically better for the DCB group compared with PTA at 6 months (one-sided P<.025)" without 12-month data. The 12-month numbers exist only in conference/news reporting (tctmd.com, which I opened): "no difference in the rate of cumulative TLR between the DCB and POBA (17.8% vs 21.8%; P = 0.39)". result.population: 1334 patients, 90 hospitals, 13 countries, randomised 2:1 to ultrathin-strut (60 um) bioresorbable-polymer sirolimus-eluting stent (Orsiro, n=884) vs thin-strut durable-polymer everolimus-eluting stent (Xience, n=450). result.reported_value: Ultrathin arm: clinically driven TLR 2.0% (vs 2.4% Xience, p=0.69); target lesion failure 6.2% (vs 9.6% Xience, p=0.04). ClinicalTrials.gov posted results for the same trial: TLF 6.32% vs 8.90%; clinically-driven TLR 17/884 (1.9%) vs 10/450 (2.2%).

VERDICT: a real primary source exists for this device class / arterial bed / timepoint, but it does not support 4.5%. The anchor should move to ~2.0%.

What was opened (three independent renderings, all read):
1. Europe PMC core record for PMID 28851504 - confirms citation (Lancet 2017;390(10105):1843-52, DOI 10.1016/S0140-6736(17)32249-3) and the 12-month TLF result (6% vs 10%, TV-MI 5% vs 8%, p=0.0155).
2. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02389946 (BIOFLOW-V) - eligibility criteria verbatim (lesion <=36 mm, RVD 2.25-4.0 mm, LM/CTO/large-side-branch bifurcation excluded) and posted results: 12-month TLF 6.32% Orsiro vs 8.90% Xience; clinically-driven TLR 17 vs 10 participants.
3. ACC clinical trial summary of BIOFLOW V - component endpoints: cardiac death 0.1% vs 0.7%, target vessel MI 4.7% vs 8.3%, clinically driven TLR 2.0% vs 2.4%.

ENDPOINT PROBLEM WITH THE ANCHOR AS WRITTEN. The model's stated endpoint prefers CD-TLR whenever a trial reports both CD-TLR and TLF. BIOFLOW-V reports both. The correct extraction for the ultrathin-DES coronary anchor is therefore CD-TLR = 2.0% at 12 months, not a TLF-scale number. The asserted 4.5% is neither the trial's CD-TLR (2.0%) nor its TLF (6.2%); it is an interpolation the author made between a TLF figure and an imagined simple-lesion discount.

THE JUSTIFICATION IS MIS-ATTRIBUTED. The author anchors on "ABSORB III metallic arm 1-y TLF 6.1%". The ABSORB III metallic/control arm is Xience, a THIN-strut (81 um) everolimus-eluting stent - it is not the des_ultrathin class this anchor is supposed to calibrate, and 6.1% there is TLF, not CD-TLR. In BIOFLOW-V the Xience comparator's own 12-month TLF was 9.6% (8.90% in the posted results), so 6.1% is not even a stable value for the thin-strut comparator across trials. The "simple-lesion subsets 3-5%" clause has no cited source and I could not find a trial or meta-analysis reporting a 4.5% 12-month figure for ultrathin DES in a type A/B1 subset; it should be treated as the author's expert interpolation, not as evidence.

CORROBORATION that 2% is the right order of magnitude: BIOFLOW VII (Ultrathin Bioresorbable Polymer Sirolimus-Eluting Stents in US Patients Undergoing Coronary Revascularization: 2-Year Outcomes, J Soc Cardiovasc Angiogr Interv 2026;5(3):104167, DOI 10.1016/j.jscai.2025.104167, PMID 41868759, read via Europe PMC), 556 US patients, mean stent length 20.2 mm: TWO-year TLF 5.2% (27/522) and ischemia-driven TLR 2.7% (14/515). A 24-month ID-TLR of 2.7% is incompatible with a 12-month CD-TLR of 4.5%. Also located but NOT opened (403/CAPTCHA blocked, so not used as evidence): Bangalore et al., Circulation 2018;138:2216-26 ultrathin-vs-thicker-strut meta-analysis (16 RCTs, 22,766 patients, 1-year TLF RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.72-0.99, driven by lower clinically indicated TLR) - a future pass with journal access could tighten the pooled absolute CD-TLR rate, which is the ideal source for this anchor.

RECOMMENDATION. Set the value to 0.02 (2.0%, 12-month clinically driven TLR, BIOFLOW-V ultrathin arm) and cite Kandzari 2017 rather than ABSORB III. Raise trust weight from 1 to 3: this is a multicentre RCT with adjudicated endpoints and a directly matching device class, bed and timepoint, but it is deliberately not weight 4-5 because (a) the population is non-complex rather than strictly type A/B1, so applying it to a simple-lesion cell is still a mild extrapolation, and (b) no source reports the simple-lesion subset separately. If the model ever needs the TLF-scale number for this cell instead, use 6.2% (0.062) with the same citation and label the endpoint explicitly as TLF - do not average the two.

result.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
result.population: Rutherford 4-6 critical limb ischaemia with infrapopliteal (below-the-knee) lesions; 358 patients randomised 2:1 to IN.PACT Amphirion paclitaxel DEB vs standard PTA; PTA control arm n=119
result.reported_value: 13.1% CD-TLR in the standard PTA (plain balloon) arm at 12 months (vs 9.2% for IN.PACT Amphirion DEB, p = 0.291)

SOURCES ACTUALLY OPENED (all via Europe PMC REST core records; PubMed and NEJM HTML were blocked by cookie wall / 403 / reCAPTCHA):

1. PRIMARY SOURCE CHOSEN - IN.PACT DEEP, Zeller et al., JACC 2014;64(15):1568-76, PMID 25301459, doi 10.1016/j.jacc.2014.06.1198. RCT, 358 patients, 2:1 DEB vs PTA, independent CEC adjudication. PTA arm CD-TLR = 13.1% at 12 months. This is the exact bed (infrapopliteal), exact device class (plain balloon angioplasty), exact endpoint (clinically driven TLR) and exact timepoint (12 months) the model asks for, from the largest RCT of the era. It is roughly HALF the asserted 25%.

2. DEBATE-BTK, Liistro et al., Circulation 2013;128(6):615-21, PMID 23797811, doi 10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.113.001811. RCT, 132 diabetic CLI patients / 158 BTK lesions. PTA arm: "target lesion revascularization" 43% (29 patients) at 12 months, binary restenosis 74%, target vessel occlusion 55%. Note the endpoint wording is plain TLR, not CD-TLR, and the trial mandated 12-month angiographic follow-up, which inflates reintervention; it is not interchangeable with adjudicated CD-TLR.

3. LIFE-BTK, Varcoe et al., N Engl J Med 2024;390(1):9-19, PMID 37888915, doi 10.1056/NEJMoa2305637 (citation confirmed via Europe PMC). Its 12-month primary endpoint is a COMPOSITE (freedom from above-ankle amputation, target-vessel occlusion, clinically driven TLR and binary restenosis): 44% freedom in the angioplasty arm vs 74% scaffold. I could NOT retrieve an isolated 12-month CD-TLR figure for the PTA arm from any source I opened, so I am not reporting one. The widely quoted 18.6% CD-TLR for the PTA arm is the 2-YEAR figure, from DeRubertis BG, Varcoe RL, Krishnan P, et al., Circulation 2025;152(15):1076-1086, doi 10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.125.075080, PMID 40927852, which I opened: "Clinically driven target lesion revascularization rates were 9.7% versus 18.6%, respectively" (DRS vs PTA, P=0.034) at 24 months. If the model's BTK-POBA anchor is meant to represent adjudicated, clinically driven reintervention - which is what the stated endpoint says - 13.1% is the defensible number and 25% is too high by roughly a factor of two. WEIGHT: raised 0.60 to 0.65 - the number can now carry a real RCT citation, but the heterogeneity across BTK POBA trials (13.1%-43%) argues against any higher confidence.

NOT FABRICATED / NOT CONFIRMED: I did not locate a 12-month CD-TLR for the LIFE-BTK PTA arm, and I have left it out rather than derive one. No DOI, PMID, volume or page in this report was guessed; each came from the Europe PMC record I fetched.

result.url_checked: https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi?db=pubmed&id=28838480&rettype=abstract&retmode=text (MEDLINE record, full abstract read); https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT01305174 (registry record read for device material and endpoint definition); https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC13092755/fullTextXML (2026 meta-analysis full text read)

(Primary endpoint was a different, larger-magnitude endpoint: duplex binary restenosis, 6.1% in the self-expanding arm.)

Corroboration: Hew & Antoniou meta-analysis (EJVES Vasc Forum 2026;65:152-161, PMID 42016495, DOI 10.1016/j.ejvsvf.2026.02.005) used a pooled self-expanding "control group proportion of 2.4%" for TLR in its trial sequential analysis (ICE + SENS-ILIAC, 718 lesions).
result.evidence_quote: "Kaplan-Meier estimate of freedom from TLR was 97.2% and 93.6%, respectively (p = 0.042)."
result.notes:
VERDICT: the anchor's endpoint attribution is right but the number is too high; 4.5% should come down to ~2.8%.

Primary source found and opened: the ICE trial (Krankenberg et al., JACC Cardiovasc Interv 2017), a 660-patient multicentre RCT — the highest tier of evidence for this cell and the trial the ESVS 2024 PAD guideline cites for preferring self-expanding stents in the iliac bed. The self-expanding arm used the PROTEGE GPS self-expanding nitinol stent (confirmed verbatim in the ClinicalTrials.gov record: "PROTEGE GPS selfexpanding nitinol stent"), so the device class se_nitinol matches exactly. The registry also confirms the TLR endpoint was specified as CLINICALLY DRIVEN, so this maps onto the model's 12-month CD-TLR endpoint without endpoint conversion.

Number: 12-month KM freedom from TLR 97.2% -> CD-TLR 2.8%. Independent corroboration from the only meta-analysis of RCTs in this space (Hew & Antoniou, EJVES Vasc Forum 2026;65:152-161, PMID 42016495 — opened via Europe PMC): its trial sequential analysis assumed a self-expanding-arm TLR "control group proportion of 2.4%", pooled over ICE + SENS-ILIAC. So two independent reads land at 2.4-2.8%, not 4.5%.

WHERE THE AUTHOR'S 4.5% PROBABLY CAME FROM — endpoint confusion. The justification note says "1-y patency loss around 5%", which is a DIFFERENT endpoint. Loss of primary patency / restenosis / TVR in the iliac bed genuinely runs near 5-6%:
- ICE self-expanding arm 12-month duplex BINARY RESTENOSIS = 6.1% (this is the trial's primary endpoint, and roughly double its CD-TLR);
- ORION pivotal single-arm trial of the EPIC self-expanding nitinol iliac stent (Clair et al., J Endovasc Ther 2014;21(2):213-222, PMID 24754280, DOI 10.1583/13-4560.1, abstract opened): "By 12 months, 6 (5.4%) of 111 patients had TVR", primary patency 94.4% — but that is TVR, not TLR, and single-arm;
- SENS-ILIAC RCT (Choi et al., Heart Vessels 2024;39(12):1060-1067, PMID 38953938, DOI 10.1007/s00380-024-02431-4, abstract opened) nitinol self-expandable arm: 1-year clinical patency 99%, "rate of repeat revascularization at 1 year ... 7.0% in the SES group" — again repeat revascularisation, and its patency assessment was judged high risk of bias in the meta-analysis because ABI/clinical judgement replaced the protocol's imaging.
So 4.5% sits in the patency-loss/TVR band, not the CD-TLR band. Keeping it would systematically inflate the iliac se_nitinol cell relative to other beds whose anchors are true CD-TLR.

CAVEATS on the suggested 2.8%: (1) ICE enrolled mostly claudicants with single, relatively simple iliac lesions, so it under-represents real-world TASC C/D and heavily calcified disease — the meta-analysis explicitly flags this limited external validity; (2) outcome assessors were unblinded (RoB2 "some concerns" for TLR), and duplex surveillance can pull some reinterventions forward; (3) it is one device (Protege). If the model needs a value that also covers complex aortoiliac lesions, 2.8% is the low end and something in the 3-4% range would be defensible — but that would be an expert blend, not a cited figure, so I am reporting the trial number.

WEIGHT: raise 0.7 -> 0.8. Justification for the higher weight: a 660-patient randomised multicentre trial, device class matched exactly, endpoint prespecified as clinically driven TLR, and a 2026 meta-analysis independently reproducing the same magnitude. Not higher than 0.8 because the evidence base is still thin (only 3 RCTs exist in this bed, GRADE certainty rated LOW for TLR, trial sequential analysis inconclusive, required information size 1508 vs 718 obtained) and the population is skewed to simple claudication lesions.

| symptom-driven TLR（1991–93 年代，无常规随访造影） | COR-POBA |
| TVF / TVR（血管级，非病变级） | COR-undersized |

时间点也不恒定：COR-BMS 是 390 天（约 13 个月）；RENAL-stent 是 312 天（约 10.3 个月）且 KM 曲线在此终止，PMA P110001 里根本不存在 12 个月再血管化终点，12 个月随访只采了血压、用药、AE、肌酐。RENAL 还是**病变级**（241 病变、39 例双侧），不是患者级。

**最致命的发现：5 个 anchor 的断言值可以从被引论文里的"另一个终点"精确还原。** 这不是笔误，是终点替换：

- SFA-long-bare 0.35 ≈ 100−64.8 = 35.2%，primary patency loss（duplex 二分再狭窄 + TLR 复合），不是 TLR（TLR 是 31.8%）
- RENAL-stent 0.14 ≈ 14.7%，9 个月二分再狭窄率的**单侧 95% 上限**（点估计 10.5%，CD-TLR 是 5.9%）
- CAR-stent 0.035 ≈ 3.8%/3.4%，ACT I 的主要**复合安全终点**（30 天死亡/卒中/MI + 1 年同侧卒中）。论文全文没有出现过 "restenosis" 一词，真实 CD-TLR 是 0.6%
- COR-POBA 0.32 ≈ 31.6%，STRESS I **支架臂**的**6 个月造影**再狭窄率（错臂、错终点、错时间点三连），或 30% 的 death/MI/any-revasc MACE
- ILIAC-stent 0.045 ≈ (2.8% CD-TLR + 6.1% duplex 再狭窄)/2 = 4.45%，两个终点取中点
- BTK-DCB 0.12 ≈ (9.2% DCB + 13.1% PTA)/2 = 11.15%，两个**试验臂**取中点

方法学审稿人十分钟就能复现这组反推。这一段单独就足以让 "endpoint is held constant" 这句话成为撤回理由。

还有一个机制层面的偏倚不是记账问题：TLF 含死亡与 MI，在竞争风险高的人群（BTK 的 Rutherford 4–6 CLI、COR-BMS 的高出血风险 75.7 岁人群，1 个月 DAPT）里，死亡和大截肢把肢体/患者从可再干预池中移除，使再血管化成分系统性偏低。把 TLF 与 CD-TLR 跨床混用，等于把基线死亡率梯度（CLI vs 无症状颈动脉）编码进了"器械失效"参数。

## 2. 应当剔除的 anchor

**必须剔除（无法修复）**

1. **COR-undersized** —— 三重错配。终点是 TVF（血管级，含非靶病变段 TVR，且定义不限 ischemia-driven）；构造是 stent under**expansion**（MSA ≤5.5 mm² 绝对切点）而非 under**sizing**（直径选择）；器械类别是混合二代 DES（Xience ~81 μm、IVUS-ACS 杂牌），不是 des_ultrathin；数量级差 5.2 倍。5.5 mm² 绝对切点把真正的选径错误与"血管本来就细"严重混淆，JACC 随刊社论已就此点名。没有任何数值可以从该文献取出，只能作为专家先验。
2. **SFA-long-bare** —— 断言值来自 patency loss；可用的 TLR 是监测驱动、无独立裁定的全因 TLR，是 CD-TLR 的上界而非估计；27% 病变累及腘动脉（不是 SFA）；均长 242 mm（150–450 mm）、全 TASC C/D、29% CLI；两中心单臂非随机。
3. **RENAL-stent** —— 源文献不存在 12 个月再血管化终点；病变级 KM；(270,312] 区间 194 个 at-risk 中 189 个删失，引用值正好落在曲线数据耗尽前最后一个台阶；SSED 与 IFU 是同一份 PMA 提交的同一数据集、表格逐字节相同，不构成两个独立来源。
4. **COR-DES-simple** —— 4.5% 在 BIOFLOW V 中不存在（任何终点、任何臂）；且该队列 73.8% 病变为 ACC/AHA B2/C、50.8% ACS、35% 糖尿病，是复杂病变试验，与 "simple" 层完全相反。要么重新找真正的 A/B1 队列，要么剔除。

**保留但须大幅降权**

5. **COR-DES-complex** —— post hoc、PS 匹配、复杂 PCI 亚组仅 336 例 19 事件、HR 95%CI 上界 11.26；HOST-IDEA 本体是 3 vs 12 个月 DAPT 试验，韩国单国选择性人群。可用 0.057，但 weight 不应高于 0.3。
6. **COR-DCB-small** —— 4.4% 约等于 116 例中 5 个事件；TLF 是次要终点，主要终点是 9 个月节段内 %DS；p=0.72 不提供任何等效性信息；方案强制成功预扩张后才给 DCB，是筛选过的 DCB 友好病变子集。
7. **COR-BMS** —— 若保留必须改成 0.098 并写明 390 天、高出血风险、1 个月 DAPT、薄支架 Gazelle、无方案规定随访造影。真正的问题是：0.16 这个量级来自有强制随访造影的旧 BMS 试验（oculostenotic reflex 驱动的 TLR），那是另一个终点构造，不能和 CD-TLR 放在同一列。同门 LEADERS FREE III 的 BMS 队列给 10.6%，独立印证该试验族的水平是 ~10% 而非 ~16%。

## 4. 存活偏倚 —— 方向与提问的假设相反，但结构性问题更严重

按 bed 统计存活率：SFA 3/4（75%）、carotid 1/1、BTK 1/2、coronary **1/7（14%）**、iliac 0/1、renal 0/1。**外周（SFA）是全集里来源最好的床，冠脉是最差的。** 提问里的假设（冠脉扎实、外周不扎实）不成立。

但真正会毁掉"跨床共享一套参数"论证的是这四点：

1. **来源不独立。** SFA-DCB 与 SFA-POBA 是 IN.PACT SFA 的两个臂，weight 各 1.0；BTK-DCB 与 BTK-POBA 是 IN.PACT DEEP 的两个臂，weight 各 0.6。16 个 anchor 中 4 个 = 2 项试验，且这 2 项试验承载了最高权重的外周信号。两项都是 Medtronic 紫杉醇 DCB RCT，共享 site mix、CEC、CD-TLR 触发定义（ABI 下降 ≥20% 或 >0.15 + 劳力性症状）、申办方。它们的误差高度相关，不能当独立残差。碰巧存活的 3 个数值里有 2 个来自同一篇。
2. **床内对比一致、跨床对比不一致。** 每个床内部的 device-vs-POBA 对比是同试验同裁定，内部自洽；但跨床梯度是假的 —— coronary POBA 来自 1991–93 年 Palmaz-Schatz 时代、symptom-driven 定义、无监测；SFA POBA 来自 2015 年、CEC 裁定 CD-TLR。模型学到的"冠脉 vs 外周"差异里混着 22 年的时代效应和终点定义效应。
3. **单 anchor 床全部建立在被替换的终点上。** carotid、iliac、renal 各只有 1 个 anchor，且三个断言值分别来自复合安全终点、两终点取中点、再狭窄率的置信上限。共享参数集在这三个床上被各一个纯人工制品钉死，任何 bed-level 随机效应都会把 artifact 吸收成"生物学差异"。
4. **权重与证据质量方向相反。** CAR-stent weight 0.8 却错 5.8×；RENAL 0.6 建立在单臂监管档案且无 12 个月终点；COR-undersized 0.4 建立在构造错配。weight 编码的是作者信心，不是审计结果。
5. **修正后的位移不对称。** 外周几乎不动（SFA-DCB 0、SFA-POBA 0、SFA-nitinol −0.003），冠脉与单 anchor 床坍塌（CAR −0.029、RENAL −0.081、COR-POBA −0.150）。也就是说未修正集夸大了非 SFA 床的失效水平、同时压低了 SFA 中 DCB 优势的表观幅度。目前"一套参数可跨床迁移"的任何拟合良好度，很可能是"SFA 之外的通胀更大"这一 artifact。

补一条会被追问的：CAR-stent 修正后是 0.6%，与零的噪声无法区分，对颈动脉再狭窄几乎不含信息；颈动脉真正有信息的终点是 duplex 再狭窄，而它不在声明的终点集里。结论是颈动脉可能根本无法在 CD-TLR 尺度上校准，该 anchor 会被平凡拟合。

**另外必须修的一个流程缺陷：survived 标志测的不是证据，是审查者的判定政策。** 6 个 anchor 出现分裂判决（COR-DES-complex、COR-BMS、SFA-long-bare、BTK-POBA、ILIAC、COR-DCB-small），每一例中两位审查者对事实完全一致，只在"数值不符是否算 refutation"上分歧 —— 一方记为 refuted，另一方记为 caveat。同时 CAR-stent 与 BTK-DCB 被标 survived=true，而其数值分别错 5.8× 和 1.3×（两位审查者都明确指出了）。必须把 **citation integrity（文献是否真实且转录正确）** 与 **value support（源文献是否报告该数值）** 拆成两列。按后者，通过率是 3/16。

## 5. 对仍属专家估计的 anchor，稿件应当怎么写

1. **删掉那句话。** 替换为逐 anchor 的终点列，至少包含七个字段：终点构造（CD-TLR / TLF / 全因 TLR / duplex 再狭窄 / TVF）、触发机制（临床 vs 方案监测）、裁定（独立 CEC / 核心室 / 无）、估计量（KM vs 粗率）、分析单位（患者 vs 病变）、实际时间窗（312 d / 12 mo / 390 d）、设计（RCT 臂 / 单臂 / post hoc 亚组）。
2. **明确声明哪些是专家先验而非文献值**，并在所有表、图中用独立符号标记。目前至少包括 COR-undersized、COR-DES-simple（作为 simple 层）、以及修正前的 COR-BMS/COR-POBA 水平。
3. **给出 elicitation 出处**：几位专家、如何提问、给出什么区间。若从未做正式征询，就写"author judgement, no formal elicitation" —— 明说比暗示有文献支撑安全得多。
4. **用先验区间和方差降权，不要用 0.4–1.0 的临时 weight。** 并提供把全部专家 anchor 剔除后的敏感性分析；若结论改变，直接写出来。
5. **不要对两个终点或两个试验臂取中点。** 存在两个候选终点时选定一个，另一个作为敏感性边界报告。ILIAC 的 0.045 与 BTK-DCB 的 0.12 都必须按此重做。
6. **披露来源不独立性**：写明 SFA 与 BTK 各贡献 1 项试验而非 2 个 anchor，并采用 trial-level 随机效应或直接合并。
7. **写明时代与监测偏倚方向**：监测驱动 TLR（SFA-long-bare、RENAL 的 duplex PSVR>2.4 阈值）系统偏高，而 1990 年代 symptom-driven TLR 在无常规造影下系统偏低 —— 两者偏倚方向相反，不可互换。
8. **量化整体位移并同时报告两版拟合**：13/16 数值改变、方向全部朝下、比值 1.0–5.8×、校准权重 74% 原先依赖未获证实的数值。主动写出这一点，比等审稿人算出来要好得多。

Of 16 anchors, only three are values the primary source actually reports at a commensurable 12-month endpoint, and two of those three are the two arms of a single trial; the remaining thirteen were stated high by factors of 1.0 to 5.8, with five traceable to a different endpoint reported in the same paper.
